Synchronize the HTTP/2 probe test's threads with a barrier (#5290)

test_http2_probe_blocked_per_thread asserts that consecutive probes come from
different threads, but ThreadPoolExecutor does not guarantee that each work
item runs on its own thread: a worker whose peers start late can take two
items in a row, so one thread probes twice and the assertion fires.

Make the three threads meet at a barrier before connecting, so each item
really does run on its own thread, and use the executor as a context manager
so its workers finish before teardown.
Fix HTTP/2 probe cache lock leak (#5254)

Return an empty bytes object from SSLTransport reads at a ragged EOF (#5279)

SSLTransport is a transcription of ssl.SSLSocket, and that class tells the
two EOF cases apart in the same except clause: a read into a buffer returns
the number of bytes written, and a read that returns the data returns b"".
_wrap_ssl_read collapses both into the integer 0, so recv() and read()
hand an int to callers that expect bytes.

ci: Compare benchmarks with the base branch on every PR

maint/benchmark/ci_benchmark.py measures CPU time per unit for the parsers
(typical and worst-case headers, cookies, header params, multipart), the
websocket mask, xhtml_escape, and the server scenarios from
dos_benchmark.py (refactored so they can be called from other scripts).

compare_benchmarks.py runs it against two source trees. Each round starts
a worker process per tree and alternates measurements between them, so
both see the same machine conditions, and keeps the fastest result for
each. Anything more than 20% slower is measured again with twice as many
processes and fails only if that agrees, since one side occasionally gets
an unusually fast or slow process.

The new CI job runs the comparison against the PR's base branch, alongside
the full tests (it takes a little over a minute), and puts the table on
the run's summary page. It also fails if an adversarial input exceeds an
absolute budget in microseconds per byte. In repeated comparisons of a
tree with itself nothing failed (one benchmark needed a recheck); a 40%
slowdown in header parsing failed on the header benchmarks only.

Return errors instead of crashing on two kinds of malformed input

Return errors instead of crashing on two kinds of malformed input

A Host header whose port has more digits than int() accepts (4300 by
default) raised ValueError from HTTPServerRequest, which was logged as an
uncaught exception and closed the connection without a response. It is
now a 400 like other invalid Host headers.

A permessage-deflate offer with an unsupported parameter, or a
max_window_bits that isn't an integer zlib accepts, failed the websocket
handshake with a 500 (plus a second exception during cleanup). The server
now declines that offer and considers the next one, as RFC 7692 section 5
requires. Compression is only enabled once both the compressor and
decompressor are created.

The compressor now rejects a window of 8 bits on every zlib version.
zlib 1.2.9 and later already did; older ones (as in manylinux2014)
silently used a 9-bit window instead, which a peer that asked for 8 bits
may be unable to decompress.
